text: Establish the kernel developer workflow for the fork: QEMU gdbstub, kgdb, early console, crash-dump analysis with drgn, documented in one page and exercised in CI.
Retain and run kselftests for every retained subsystem in the nightly test matrix.

lens: Legal, licensing and governance
text: Publish a kernel dependency license allowlist that forbids Apache-2.0-only, CDDL and other GPLv2-incompatible code, requires vendored Rust crates to be taken under their MIT option, and enforce it in CI.
rationale: The Rust ecosystem defaults to MIT OR Apache-2.0 and Apache-2.0 alone is GPLv2-incompatible, so one unchecked crate can make the kernel undistributable.

lens: Legal, licensing and governance
text: Require SPDX-License-Identifier headers on every source file and gate merges on a license-header linter.
rationale: Per-file license clarity is the basis for every later scan, SBOM and compliance claim.

lens: Legal, licensing and governance
text: Enforce Signed-off-by and verified commit signatures in CI on every merged commit.
rationale: Provenance policy is worthless unless mechanically enforced.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Decide the repository topology (single monorepo containing kernel fork, native userspace, SDK and tooling vs. multiple repositories with a pinned manifest) and record it as an ADR before any second repository is created.
rationale: Every CI, versioning, bisection and release-promotion design downstream depends on whether a commit identifies the whole system or only one part of it.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Decide the top-level build orchestrator for a mixed C+Rust kernel and Rust-first userspace (Kbuild driven by Cargo workspaces, Bazel/Buck2, or a derivation-based builder aligned with the content-addressed store) and record trade-offs as an ADR.
rationale: The build orchestrator determines whether reproducibility, remote caching and hermeticity are properties of the system or bolt-ons that fight it for years.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Standardise on LLVM/Clang as the sole C compiler for the kernel fork and document GCC kernel builds as unsupported.
rationale: Rust-in-kernel requires bindgen against libclang and mixing GCC-built C with rustc-built Rust creates ABI and sanitizer mismatches that double the test matrix.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Define a pinned Rust toolchain policy for kernel code: exact rustc version, the allowed set of unstable features, an upgrade cadence tied to upstream Rust-for-Linux, and a CI job that builds with the next candidate toolchain.
rationale: Kernel Rust still depends on unstable features and an unmanaged toolchain bump can break the build for every contributor at once.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Deliver a cross-compilation bootstrap from a Linux host that produces a bootable image, then achieve self-hosted builds of the complete system on JakeOS by V1.
rationale: §61 makes daily-driving mandatory and developers cannot daily-drive an OS they must leave to rebuild.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Make every build run inside a hermetic sandbox with pinned, content-addressed inputs and no network access after dependency fetch, using the native environment primitive (§35) once it exists and a Linux-host equivalent before then.
rationale: Reproducible builds and trustworthy provenance are impossible if builds can read ambient host state.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Achieve bit-for-bit reproducible builds for the kernel, all native packages, the SDK and complete system generation images, verified by at least two independent rebuilders per release.
rationale: Content-addressed package identity (§27) and supply-chain trust are meaningless if the same source yields different bytes.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Eliminate non-determinism sources in Rust and C output (build paths, timestamps, codegen-units, incremental compilation, hash seeds, embedded absolute paths) and add a CI job that builds twice and diffs artifacts on every merge.
rationale: Reproducibility regresses one commit at a time and only a continuous double-build check prevents rediscovering the problem at release.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Define the third-party dependency policy: committed lockfiles, a vendored source mirror for all crates and C dependencies, cargo-deny licence and advisory checks in CI, and a review requirement for new dependencies.
rationale: Hermetic builds need offline sources and an OS must not ship a crate it cannot audit or rebuild if crates.io disappears.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Deploy a shared content-addressed remote build cache (compiler cache plus artifact cache) usable by CI and by developers, with cache hits verified against reproducible outputs.
rationale: A kernel plus userspace plus compatibility layers is too large to rebuild from scratch on every CI run without making pre-merge feedback unusably slow.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Set and track build-time budgets: incremental kernel rebuild under 2 minutes, incremental native userspace rebuild under 1 minute, full clean CI build under 30 minutes on the reference runner.
rationale: Build latency directly determines contributor throughput and whether people run tests before pushing.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Define build profiles (debug with lockdep/KASAN/KCSAN/UBSAN/KFENCE and Rust debug assertions, release with LTO and stripped symbols, and a symbols-preserved release variant) and run the debug profile in nightly CI.
rationale: Memory-safety bugs in inherited C and unsafe Rust are only caught if sanitized kernels are actually booted and exercised regularly.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Decide the linker (lld vs. mold), LTO scope and PGO policy for kernel and userspace, and measure their effect on the §54 benchmarks before adopting them.
rationale: Link-time choices affect binary size, startup latency and reproducibility, and PGO in particular threatens bit-for-bit builds.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Keep an ARM64 kernel and userspace cross-build compiling in CI (boot not required) even though ARM64 is not a supported platform before 1.0.
rationale: §38 forbids fossilising on x86-64 and a build that has silently become x86-only is far harder to un-break later than one that never compiles elsewhere.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Decide the CI platform with the explicit requirement of self-hosted bare-metal runners exposing KVM and connected to the hardware lab, and treat hosted runners as acceptable only for lint and unit tests.
rationale: Boot, graphics, performance and hardware testing all need nested virtualisation or real devices that hosted CI cannot provide.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Manage all CI and lab infrastructure as code with documented disaster recovery so the entire build and test pipeline can be recreated from the repository plus backups.
rationale: A years-long project will lose machines, accounts and people, and unrecoverable CI is a project-ending risk.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Structure CI into tiers: pre-merge (lint, unit, QEMU smoke boot under 15 minutes), post-merge (full QEMU matrix), nightly (sanitizers, fuzzing, performance, hardware lab) and release qualification.
rationale: A single monolithic pipeline is either too slow to gate merges or too shallow to catch regressions.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Enforce a merge queue on the main branch so every landed commit was tested against the exact tree it landed on, with no direct pushes.
rationale: Bisection and the generated roll-up progress tables assume main is always green and every commit is attributable to a passing run.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Define the QEMU/KVM test matrix: q35 machine, OVMF with and without Secure Boot, TPM emulation, virtio block/net/gpu/input/sound, CPU counts of 1, 2, 8 and 64, memory from 512 MB to 64 GB, and multi-node NUMA topologies.
rationale: Scheduling, memory-object locality and boot paths behave differently across these axes and only a declared matrix makes coverage auditable.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Build a boot test harness that drives QEMU and lab machines to a boot-complete marker over serial, detects kernel panics and Rust panics, enforces timeouts, and exercises reboot, kexec and generation-selection cycles.
rationale: The kernel fork is the foundation and a boot regression must be detected within one CI cycle, not by a developer noticing.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Build a guest-side test agent for the native userspace image that runs test components, streams structured results out over virtio-serial or vsock, and maps test failures to task IDs from the Markdown repository.
rationale: Integration tests of components, channels and capabilities must run inside the booted OS and report machine-readable results to CI.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Produce reproducible test images per milestone (minimal execution-model image for V0, desktop image from V0.5) via a single image builder shared with release engineering.
rationale: Test images that diverge from shipped images test the wrong thing.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Build the end-to-end GUI test harness on semantic interfaces (§42) and the accessibility tree rather than pixel or coordinate scripting, with pixel-based golden-image tests reserved for compositor rendering correctness.
rationale: The project's own principle is that semantic interfaces beat GUI scraping, and dogfooding that in the test harness proves the interfaces are complete.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Publish a flaky-test policy: automatic quarantine after a defined flake rate, at most one retry, a time-boxed deflake obligation on the owning workstream, and quarantine expiry that deletes or fixes the test.
rationale: Unmanaged flakes erode trust in CI until people merge on red, which destroys the value of every other gate.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Deploy a test results database and dashboard (KernelCI-style) recording per-commit, per-configuration and per-machine outcomes with history, flake rate and duration trends.
rationale: Years of results across a hardware matrix cannot be understood from individual CI logs.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Measure code coverage for kernel (kcov/gcov and Rust coverage) and userspace, and set minimum coverage gates for capability enforcement, ABI entry points and IDL-generated code paths.
rationale: Security-critical paths need evidence of exercise, not assumptions.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Enforce static analysis gates in pre-merge CI: rustfmt and clippy with warnings denied, sparse and smatch for inherited C, cargo-deny, an adapted checkpatch, and Miri for unsafe userspace Rust where feasible.
rationale: Style and lint disagreements are cheapest to settle mechanically at the first commit.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Adapt syzkaller to the native ABI: syzlang descriptions for object handles, typed channels, operations and memory objects, a capability-aware executor that can obtain and derive capabilities, and a custom program generator that understands handle ownership transfer.
rationale: Stock syzkaller cannot express typed, capability-scoped calls and the native ABI is exactly where novel kernel bugs will live.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Run continuous fuzzing infrastructure (syzbot-like) with crash deduplication, reproducer minimisation, automatic bisection and automatic task filing into the Markdown repository.
rationale: Fuzzing without triage automation produces a crash backlog nobody works.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Build a fault-injection framework that kills userspace services (compositor, audio, network, device management) and injects kernel allocation and I/O failures during test runs to verify §32 restart and rebind semantics.
rationale: Recovery that is never exercised in CI will not work when it matters.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Migrate CI runners themselves to run on JakeOS by V2 so the build and test infrastructure is dogfooded alongside the desktop.
rationale: Self-hosting the infrastructure exposes server-shaped gaps (unattended operation, remote management) that desktop dogfooding never will.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Automate dependency update proposals (crates, C libraries, firmware, QEMU, upstream Linux) as CI-validated changes with a documented review cadence.
rationale: Manual dependency tracking across a kernel fork and a Rust ecosystem falls behind within months.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Mirror all upstream sources (Linux, crates, firmware, Wine, toolchain) in project-controlled storage keyed by content hash.
rationale: Reproducing a release years later requires the inputs to still exist.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Do not build or maintain a custom compiler or forked LLVM; carry only minimal, upstream-bound patches against rustc and LLVM.
rationale: Compiler maintenance would consume the engineering budget §56.4 already commits to kernel maintenance.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Do not support building the OS from Windows or macOS hosts natively before 1.0; provide a containerised Linux build environment for those hosts instead.
rationale: Every additional host platform multiplies toolchain and reproducibility work for little contributor gain before a public release.

lens: Build, toolchain, CI and test infrastructure
text: Investigate using native components and resource domains as the isolation unit for parallel test execution (one component per test) once the primitives are stable.
rationale: Using the OS's own cheap isolation for its test harness is both a performance win and a continuous proof that §10 creation cost targets hold.

lens: Release engineering and operations
text: Decide whether the repository accepts prebuilt binaries from publishers or rebuilds every package from source on project infrastructure.
rationale: This determines whether reproducibility, SBOMs and supply-chain guarantees are project-wide or publisher-dependent.

lens: Release engineering and operations
text: Generate an SBOM (SPDX or CycloneDX) for every package and system generation from the content-addressed dependency graph.
rationale: Vulnerability matching and license compliance both require knowing exactly what is in a generation.

lens: Release engineering and operations
text: Build an embargoed build path that can compile, sign and stage a security release privately before public publication.
rationale: Public CI leaks embargoed fixes before coordinated disclosure.

lens: Release engineering and operations
text: Run a symbol server keyed by content hash (debuginfod-compatible) so stripped generations can be symbolicated on demand.
rationale: Debugging a daily-driven V1 build and every later crash report requires symbols for immutable binaries.

lens: Release engineering and operations
text: Build a physical hardware lab with remote power control, serial and video capture that boots every nightly on each Tier 1 device and runs install, suspend/resume and GPU smoke tests.
rationale: QEMU cannot catch the GPU, firmware and power regressions that break real laptops.

lens: Release engineering and operations
text: Build the install media pipeline: signed, reproducible ISO/USB images per channel with published checksums, nightly builds and automated boot tests of the produced image.
rationale: Developers cannot daily-drive V1 without a repeatable way to produce installable images.

lens: Release engineering and operations
text: Verify reproducible builds with independent rebuilders and publish per-generation reproducibility status.
rationale: Reproducibility is only a guarantee when someone other than the release pipeline reproduces the bits.

lens: Release engineering and operations
text: Document and CI-test building the entire OS from source both on a Linux host and on the OS itself, with the contributor path kept to a small fixed number of steps.
rationale: Self-hosting is the V1 goal and onboarding friction decides whether contributors stay.

lens: Migration, adoption and interoperability
text: Provide a one-command reproducible build of the kernel fork and system image from a mainstream Linux host, documented as the contributor entry point.
rationale: OS contributors must be productive before the OS can self-host, and the build path is the first thing they hit.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Establish a fuzzing program for the native ABI (syzkaller-style descriptions generated from the IDL) that runs continuously from the first ABI prototype.
rationale: Kernel ABI bugs found after freeze become permanent compatibility hazards or CVEs.

text: Decide the language policy: Rust for all new kernel and platform code, C retained only where inherited Linux code remains appropriate (ADR with criteria for when a C subsystem may be rewritten).
Establish Rust-in-kernel build support (toolchain, bindings, Kbuild integration) so native kernel subsystems can be written in Rust from V0.
Boot the forked kernel unmodified in behaviour on QEMU and on the reference x86-64 hardware as the first kernel task.
Content addressing must support reproducibility checks: a rebuilt package must be verifiable as bit-identical by hash (cross-ref BLD reproducible builds).
Build a chaos test suite that kills each restartable service under load and verifies clients rebind within a bounded time.
Validate ABI architecture-neutrality by building the native ABI headers and a smoke component for a non-x86 target (ARM64 or RISC-V) in CI without shipping it.
Run a Linux compatibility conformance suite (LTP, glibc tests, selected application smoke tests) in CI.
Define and run a Linux GUI compatibility test matrix (e.g. Firefox, LibreOffice, GIMP, VS Code, Steam client) in CI or nightly hardware runs.
Define and run a Windows compatibility test matrix of representative games and applications.
Establish Rust-in-kernel infrastructure (toolchain pinning, bindings to inherited C subsystems, build integration) for the fork.
Establish an unsafe-code policy and tooling (unsafe inventory, lint gates, forbid(unsafe_code) by default in SDK templates).
Fuzz the native kernel ABI and IDL deserialisers continuously in CI.
CI must execute the core benchmark suite on fixed reference hardware or a pinned QEMU configuration and fail merges that regress beyond threshold.
Hardware regression matrix in CI that exercises DRM, PCI, USB, NVMe, networking and ACPI on QEMU and on every reference machine for every kernel change.
Divergence measurement tooling reporting patch count, touched subsystems and merge-conflict hotspots against upstream per release.
CI lint for native ABI and SDK headers that rejects POSIX-shaped names (open/read/write/fork/ioctl), Linux syscall numbers, and Wayland protocol objects in native surfaces.
Automated V0 demo runs in CI under QEMU with recorded metrics published to the performance dashboard.
The full OS build (kernel, platform, apps, packages) completes reproducibly when run on the OS itself.
ABI conformance and cross-version compatibility test suite run in CI.
Tooling that classifies every public symbol/interface into a stability layer and enforces the layer's policy in CI.
